newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat succession up to syndicate -Agnelli.
newsitem.headline: Fiat succession up to syndicate -Agnelli.

text.p: Fiat's syndicate of major shareholders will have to decide who succeeds Cesare Romiti as chairman of the Italian industrial group, Umberto Agnelli said.
The sydicate comprises Agnelli holding companies IFI and IFIL, insurer Generali, merchant bank Mediobanca and German banking group Deutsche Bank.

"The syndicate decides, we are one of the members. The question of who takes over will have to be assessed by the existing syndicate," Agnelli told reporters attending the annual general meeting of IFIL, the family holding company of which he is chairman.
Romiti said last week after Fiat's AGM that he was sticking by his plan to retire as chairman in June 1998 when he turned 75.
Former Fiat chairman Gianni Agnelli stepped down ahead of his 75th birthday in March 1996. Both are acting in accordance with Fiat rules on the retirement of directors.
